takeaways: Other Reportable bottom 10% is the strongest bullish reset signal in the NQ sample.
High Asset Manager exposure works more like trend sponsorship than a short signal.
Low Leveraged Money can be squeeze fuel if price action remains strong.
Other Reportable high is the main medium-term caution flag.
nq.bottom_line: For NQ, do not treat high Asset Manager exposure as bearish by itself. Watch Other Reportable extremes and Leveraged Money underexposure.

takeaways: Asset Manager top 10% is a crowding warning for 13-26 week reward/risk.
Leveraged Money top 10% is the strongest long-term warning in the S&P sample.
Non-reportable top 10% has weaker forward returns; bottom 10% is the strongest bullish reset.
sp500.bottom_line: For S&P 500, Asset Manager crowding is more meaningful. Current reward/risk weakens when price action starts diverging from crowded positioning.
